questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer to you than vehicles from your right. Always check that the path is clear across the entire intersection before moving.

questions.question: If you are inside an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Keep moving at a steady pace and safely exit the intersection.
Speed up so you don't cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving at a steady pace and safely exit the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already inside an intersection when the light turns yellow, continue moving at a steady pace to safely clear the intersection.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Try to stop heavy bleeding by applying direct pressure. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks or buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and space to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you are tired.
Areas on the road that you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas on the road that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle for objects. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
A right turn is allowed on a green arrow only.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs have a yellow or yellow-green background. These signs alert you to upcoming conditions, such as curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: As it gets dark, what lights should you use so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights as daylight fades to help others see you. Use high beam headlights only in open areas where no other drivers are present.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: When is it important to check traffic behind you?
questions.explanation: Check the traffic behind you at least every 10 seconds. This is important when changing lanes, backing up, slowing down, or driving down steep hills.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on three things: your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch carefully for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain or fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What is a major cause of crashes that result in death or serious injury?

options.text: Drivers carrying more than one child.
Drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Drivers making frequent stops to rest on long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. This is a major cause of crashes resulting in death and serious injury.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can proceed without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all vehicles must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave to you.
Only if pedestrians are not texting.

questions.explanation: Always stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You may proceed carefully only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed because you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection. Wait until the pedestrian has completely crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: When you see a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, you should yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A pedestrian with a disability using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that shows a law you must obey. Right turns are not permitted where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Drivers should be careful when passing large vehicles and should not drive beside them for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Avoid driving next to a large vehicle for long periods. It is safer to drop back or move ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you an unsafe driver?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular checkups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train completely passes before crossing the tracks.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train completely passes before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop for a red or yellow light or to handle cross traffic.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What should a driver do before turning right at a red light?

options.text: Slow down and go if the way is clear, without stopping.
Stop completely, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot. Before turning, come to a complete stop, look both ways, and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, what documents must you show?
questions.explanation: You must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. All three documents are required to be in your vehicle when driving.
